result.keywords: This study examines adaptive congestion signaling mechanisms for socially-aware transport in wireless ad-hoc mesh networks. We compare loss-based and rate-based control signals under varying bandwidth, delay, and mobility conditions, and evaluate a hybrid controller that blends congestion-window tracing with delay-aware rate estimation. A measurement framework similar to prior Internet census tools is used to classify flows by control behavior, while localized bottlenecks and randomized link disruptions are introduced to test robustness. Results indicate that hybrid approaches can improve fairness and stability in dynamic multi-hop settings and may support future rate-aware variants for mobile edge deployments.
result.title: Adaptive congestion signaling for socially-aware transport in wireless ad-hoc meshes
